title: FTC Robotics — Team Araxys (#29224)

longDesc: I joined FIRST Tech Challenge in June 2025 and became an official Team Araxys member from the start of Grade 11 through about a month after Nationals. Araxys competes in the Decode season, where student teams design, build and program a robot to complete a themed game.

title: Mentoring Avengers Army
desc: Hands-on mentorship of Avengers Army, an FTC team of deaf and mute students, through Team Araxys — robotics concepts, competition prep and technical guidance, with instruction adapted to be visual and hands-on.
meta: 30–40 hours across the season · The team won Regionals and placed Top 25 at FTC Nationals
longDesc: Avengers Army is an FTC team made up of deaf and mute students. Coaching them meant rethinking how I explain technical material — moving from a purely verbal walkthrough toward visual references, diagrams, and hands-on demonstration, coordinated through interpreters and written notes.

Over the season I worked with the team on robot design decisions, build strategy, and staying composed and adaptive during competition, where matches often demand fast strategy changes that are harder to communicate under time pressure.
highlights: Coached robot design, build strategy, and competition prep
Adapted instruction to be fully visual / hands-on
30–40 hours of direct mentorship through Team Araxys
The team won Regionals and placed Top 25 at FTC Nationals

title: Drone Internship — Thanos Technologies
desc: A one-month internship at Thanos Technologies, a drone company in Hyderabad — drone marketing alongside hands-on technical understanding of different drone types and what they do.
longDesc: Over a month at a drone company in Hyderabad I saw both sides of the industry: how drones are marketed, and how different drone types are built, wired and used.

Hands-on time included frame assembly, motor wiring and soldering on agricultural-grade hexacopters, plus airfoil geometry work in CAD — a practical base for my Extended Essay research on glide ratios.

desc: A 2-day hands-on workshop covering practical drone flight training, flight simulations and introductory aerospace/UAV concepts. A foundational program covering drone flight, flight simulation, aerodynamics, and aviation fundamentals — first hands-on exposure to UAV systems.
longDesc: A foundational program at the Telangana State Aviation Academy covering drone flight, flight simulation, aerodynamics, and aviation fundamentals — my first hands-on exposure to UAV systems, and the starting point for what became my Extended Essay research direction.

title: Extended Essay — Glide Ratios & Flight Performance
desc: An aerospace-focused Extended Essay investigating glide ratio and its effect on flight performance, connecting aerodynamic theory to data gathered through flight testing.
longDesc: My IB Extended Essay investigates how glide ratio affects flight performance, connecting aerodynamic theory — lift-to-drag ratio, wing loading, airfoil shape — to data gathered through actual flight testing rather than simulation alone.
The research draws directly on what I learned in the drone workshop and UAV internship, using those flight sessions as a source of real test data for the essay.
highlights: Combines aerodynamic theory with flight-test data

title: Pollination Robot
desc: An autonomous pollination robot concept addressing declining bee populations, developed for the Imperial College London Stemathon and the University of Sydney India Innovation Challenge. Led the presentation strategy, opening hook, and judge networking, and built out the research, engineering concept, pitch video, and business proposal.
meta: Round 2 at Imperial STEMathon · Special Mention Award, India Innovation Challenge · Internship completed at Technic Education
longDesc: An autonomous pollination robot concept addressing declining bee populations, built for the Imperial College London Stemathon and the University of Sydney India Innovation Challenge — a small robot meant to supplement natural pollination in agricultural settings where bee populations are stressed or absent.

I led the presentation strategy — the opening hook, structuring the pitch, and judge networking — and also built out the research, engineering concept, pitch video, and business proposal, so the project spanned both the technical concept and how it was communicated to judges.
highlights: Reached Round 2 at Imperial College London Stemathon
Summer internship at Technic Education (Grade 10): engineering design & prototyping, completion letter received
Special Mention Award — India Innovation Challenge
Built research, engineering concept, pitch video & business proposal
Co-authoring a literature review on declining bee populations and robotic pollination (in progress)

title: Cryptic Claws
desc: A self-written and illustrated educational graphic novel for grade 5–6 students — a mystery story where the detective breaks the fourth wall to teach the math concept needed to solve each case. Originally created as my MYP Personal Project.
meta: Requested by the school counsellor for use with specially-abled students · Being refined for publication
longDesc: A self-written and illustrated educational graphic novel for grade 5–6 students, built around a detective who breaks the fourth wall to teach the math concept needed to solve each mystery. It started as my MYP Personal Project and has grown from there.

The school counsellor has requested it for use with specially-abled students, since the visual, narrative format makes abstract math concepts more approachable than a standard worksheet. I'm currently refining it for wider publication.

title: Lucky Number 30
desc: A self-designed mathematics card game where players race to reach exactly 30 using cards from ±1 to ±13, with wild and "remove last card" mechanics that add real-time arithmetic challenge.
meta: Playtested with 50–60+ students across school events · Expanding with multiplication/division and an online version
longDesc: A self-designed math card game where players race to reach exactly 30 using cards numbered ±1 to ±13, with wild cards and a "remove last card" mechanic that forces real-time arithmetic and strategic thinking.
I playtested it with 50+ students to tune the difficulty and pacing, and it's since been used in math and design events at school.
highlights: Expanding with multiplication/division mechanics and an online playable version
